text.p: French championship matches this weekend (last season's final position in brackets, kickoff times GMT):
Playing Friday, kickoff 1630
Toulouse (promoted) v Rennes (16)

Back in the top flight after three seasons in the second division, Toulouse are coached by former international playmaker Alain Giresse. Their most noteworthy close-season signing was South African Ernest Mtawali. After a lacklustre 1996-97 season, Rennes have been amply revamped with 14 new faces in the side but they lost last season's top marksman Stephane Guivarc'h.
Playing Friday, kickoff 1830
Monaco (1) v Bordeaux (4)

Despite losing some key names -- Sonny Anderson, Patrick Blondeau and Emmanuel Petit for instance -- and a number of injuries, notably Scot John Collins, reigning champions Monaco start the season as favourites. The Bordeaux match will be a first test for former Nantes striker Japhet N'Doram. Bordeaux look among the leading outsiders with an impressive recruiting drive but the team may still be a little makeshift.
Playing Saturday, kick off 1800 all matches
Guingamp (12) v Cannes (15)

Both teams expected to struggle this season. Guingamp have surprised by staying two seasons in the top flight and the Bretons have lost two of their most gifted players, Stephane Carnot and Liberia's Christopher Wreh. The situation is even worse for Cannes and new Dutch coach Addick Koot, who have to rely on a mostly inexperienced squad.
Lens (13) v Auxerre (6)

Both sides hope to avenge a very disappointing season. Lens' striking power should be improved by the arrivals of Montenegro's marksman Anto Drobnjak and playmaker Stephane Ziani. Champions in 1996, Auxerre have replaced centre-forward Lilian Laslandes by Stephane Guivarc'h. Having played tough Intertoto matches, the Burgundy team should be in better early season shape.
Lyon (8) v Metz (5)

Lyon strengthened their defence, hoping to make an impact after two promising seasons. Played well in recent Intertoto matches. Metz remain one of the most solid French sides, a haven of stability in a world of big money and transfer disputes. They even managed to keep brilliant striker Robert Pires, who was courted by most big clubs in Europe.
Marseille (11) v Le Havre (14)

With the help of Marseille-born Rolland Courbis, back in his first club 25 years after being dismissed as a player, Marseille hope to erase once and for all traces of their troubled past. Their recruiting looks wise enough to bring them back near the top, especially as they are not playing in Europe. Le Havre, who won in Marseille last year, hope to be among the leading upset specialists this season. Loss of goalkeeper Christophe Revault, midfielders Frederic Brando and Teddy Bertin, both to Marseille, will not help.
Montpellier (10) v Strasbourg (9)

Both sides looked promising last year, Strasbourg winning the League Cup while Montpellier narrowly missed direct qualification to the UEFA Cup. Both made few changes this season and should be among the teams to watch.
Nantes (3) v Bastia (7)

Nantes have again lost most of their best players and the Canaries, champions in 1995, hope the annual achievement of building an efficient team from scratch will happen again. Coach Jean-Claude Suaudeau resigned and his assistant Reynald Denoueix has taken over. Bastia lost striker Anto Drobnjak and Slovak playmaker Lubomir Moravcik but could surprise once more.
Paris St Germain (2) v Chateauroux (promoted)

Paris St Germain start as favourites for the fourth consecutive season after having finished second three times. Another failure would not be tolerated by fans and team officials have done they can to avoid it, recruiting gifted Florian Maurice and Franck Gava from Lyon and Marco Simone from AC Milan. Their opening tie against Chateauroux is symbolic as the newly-promoted side, who were until recently chaired by PSG's president Michel Denisot, have long been considered PSG's reserve side.
